scope: Provider-native goals and owned Codex automatic goal turns; this is not full headless parity.
implemented: Codex show/edit/clear/pause/resume/set controls use native APIs, with case-sensitive command prefix, Unicode whitespace and attachment guards.
Set validates at most 4000 Unicode scalar characters before reading or mutating a native goal, preserving the existing goal on local rejection.
Set installs a paused goal, starts the first turn with captured model/effort/approval/sandbox/plan settings, then activates the goal; resume uses empty native input.
Automatic native turns remain within one owning app run and attempt, with distinct terminal provider turns and completed assistant messages.
The upstream five-second continuation grace pauses an uncontinued active goal before app completion; Stop pauses and interrupts the current native turn or releases an already-ended turn.
Pending activation does not block Stop; late acknowledgements and orphan starts cannot revive detached work. Goal notifications win over older request snapshots.
Explicit command provenance is derived from the app message creator. Cleanup pauses are automatic; installed Codex 0.166 and 0.167 interoperate.
Control-only turns have no native rollback reference and derive their identity from the owning attempt.
Claude synthetic goal confirmations and Stop-hook feedback update the provider-thread projection. Only a checked successful root completes the goal; child output and failed turns do not.
Fixed-shape native goal validation errors use upstream actionable wording, and failed goal replacement publishes the last observed cleared/paused state.
Common test fixtures allocate fresh random paths without recursively deleting a previous tree.
